title: Capacity postmortem extract - regional queueing & throttle breakdown
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an extract used by infra + SRE to validate the Capacity Incident postmortem hypotheses (Mar 12-14 2026): specifically to quantify regional GPU saturation, per-request queueing distribution, and which throttle classes triggered during the incident windows.

Time window and granularity:
- Primary window: 2026-03-12T04:00:00Z -> 2026-03-14T12:00:00Z
- Granularity: 5m rollups per region / AZ / GPU sku / queue-class

Data sources (tables queried):
- bigquery:prod_infra.usage.gpu_allocation_rollups_5m
- bigquery:prod_infra.telemetry.request_queues_5m
- bigquery:prod_infra.policy.throttle_events
- bigquery:prod_infra.autoscaler.events

Columns included in this extract (CSV below):
region,availability_zone,gpu_type,timestamp_start,timestamp_end,total_gpus,reserved_gpus,free_gpus,avg_gpu_util_pct,p50_queue_ms,p95_queue_ms,p99_queue_ms,throttled_reqs,throttle_pct,throttle_class,autoscaler_events,primary_cause_notes

Sample rows (derived from rollups):
us-west1,us-west1-a,A100-80GB,2026-03-12T04:00:00Z,2026-03-12T04:05:00Z,120,20,0,93.4,12,240,980,2120,12.1%,rate-limit-tiering,scale_up_delayed:cooldown_stuck,observed steady high sustained seq-length workloads + no prefix cache hit
us-west1,us-west1-a,A100-80GB,2026-03-12T20:10:00Z,2026-03-12T20:15:00Z,120,20,0,98.8,18,820,2800,7450,32.4%,global-burst-throttle,scale_up_failed:max_nodes,large PLs from a single customer causing queueing and local saturation
europe-west1,europe-west1-b,A100-40GB,2026-03-13T02:00:00Z,2026-03-13T02:05:00Z,64,8,4,67.1,6,42,90,0,0.0%,none,scale_up_normal,brief localized spike (traffic rerouted from us-west during incident)
ap-southeast1,ap-southeast1-c,A40-80GB,2026-03-14T09:25:00Z,2026-03-14T09:30:00Z,48,4,0,88.2,10,360,1500,430,6.8%,quota-throttle,scale_up_delayed:insufficient_quota,autoscaler not allowed to request more instances due to project quota

Derived metrics notes:
- "free_gpus" = total_gpus - reserved_gpus - allocated_gpus (allocated inferred from avg_utilization model). Some rows use approximate allocation for labelled best-effort pools.
- throttle_pct = throttled_reqs / (throttled_reqs + served_reqs) aggregated per rollup window.

Key SQL snippets used to produce this sheet (sanitized):
-- rollup GPU allocation + utilization
SELECT region,az,gpu_sku,window_start,window_end, SUM(total_gpus) as total_gpus, SUM(reserved) as reserved_gpus, AVG(avg_gpu_util_pct) as avg_gpu_util_pct
FROM `prod_infra.usage.gpu_allocation_rollups_5m`
WHERE window_start BETWEEN TIMESTAMP('2026-03-12') AND TIMESTAMP('2026-03-14 23:59:59')
GROUP BY region,az,gpu_sku,window_start,window_end

-- queue distribution per request class
SELECT region,az,queue_class,window_start,quantiles(queue_latency_ms, [0.5,0.95,0.99]) as q
FROM `prod_infra.telemetry.request_queues_5m`
WHERE window_start BETWEEN ...

-- throttle events join to map classes to counts
SELECT t.region,t.az,t.window_start, SUM(t.count) as throttled_reqs, ANY_VALUE(t.throttle_class) as throttle_class
FROM `prod_infra.policy.throttle_events` t
GROUP BY t.region,t.az,t.window_start

Observations & rapid conclusions (data-backed):
1) High-latency queueing coincides with windows where free_gpus==0 and avg_gpu_util_pct >= 90% for >= 30 minutes in us-west1 primary AZs. p95 queue latency > 700ms in those windows.
2) Two distinct throttle modes contributed: (a) global-burst safety throttle (applied to cross-customer traffic during sustained spike) and (b) per-account rate-tier throttles for the affected customer. Global-burst accounted for ~60% of throttled_reqs during peak windows.
3) Autoscaler signals were generated but the scale-up actions either failed (quota) or were delayed due to cooldown rules and a recent controller config change that increased the evaluation window.
4) Traffic spillover to europe-west1 happened but those regions had lower utilization and acted as partial pressure relief; however cross-region routing lag meant relief came late.

Data quality caveats:
- Some A/B test clusters report 'gpu_sku' as NULL in older rollups; rows flagged when gpu_sku is NULL were backfilled heuristically.
- Reserved capacity reported by dedicated pools sometimes counts warm standby nodes; we mark those with reserved_gpus > 0 and note in primary_cause_notes.

Suggested next actions (owner + ETA):
- [ACTION] Short-term: Increase emergency reserved capacity in us-west1 by +16 A100 nodes for 72h to stabilize (owner: Priya Nair, ETA: 2026-03-22).
- [ACTION] Medium-term: Revert autoscaler evaluation window change and set cooldown to 30s (owner: Luis Ortega, ETA: 2026-04-01).
- [ACTION] Instrument per-request prefix cache hit ratio in the rollups (owner: Ben Hollis, ETA: 2026-03-28).
- [ACTION] Add synthetic traffic and canary for cross-region routing logic to detect lag earlier (owner: eng-sre, ETA: 2026-04-05).

Open questions for follow-up:
- Was the global-burst throttle threshold too aggressive for sustained but legitimate traffic patterns? (ask policy team).
- Can we make autoscaler quota fallback path more transparent in alerts?

Pointer to complete raw exports:
- BigQuery job ids and exported CSVs are attached to Jira INFRA-1247. Use the bq export job ids in linked artifacts.

Sheet maintenance notes:
- This extract is intended to be an immutable snapshot for the incident. For daily ops, use monitoring dashboards under infra -> capacity -> gpu-rollups.

End of extract.
